identity.title: A Spatially Resolved Study of Cold Dust, Molecular Gas, H II Regions, and Stars in the z = 2.12 Submillimeter Galaxy ALESS67.1

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present detailed studies of a $z=2.12$ submillimeter galaxy, ALESS67.1, using sub-arcsecond resolution ALMA, AO-aided VLT/SINFONI, and *HST*/CANDELS data

evidence.quote: ALESS67.1 has a spectroscopic redshift at $z_{\rm spec}=2.1230$ (cite: Danielson:2017aa)
ALESS67.1 has a spectroscopic redshift at $z_{\rm spec}=2.1230$ (cite: Danielson:2017aa)

question.value: How do the sizes, spatial distributions and kinematics of dust, CO gas, H II regions and stars compare in the z=2.12 SMG ALESS67.1, and what does this imply for alpha_CO, IRX-beta and the Schmidt-Kennicutt relation?

evidence.quote: we find a factor of 4–6 smaller sizes in dust continuum compared to all the other tracers, including $^{12}$CO, and UV and H$\alpha$ emission is significantly offset from the dust continuum.

analysis_steps.goal: Image Band 7 continuum and measure flux and size

method.value: Natural-weight dirty image, clean a 1'' circle to 2 sigma; uvmodelfit Gaussian fit to the uv data, cross-checked with imfit and sextractor

evidence.quote: we first use the uvmodelfit algorithm to model the *uv*–data. We find that the best bit (reduced $\chi^2$=0.5) Gaussian profile has an intensity of 3.7$\pm$0.2 mJy

fitting.value: Gaussian profile, chi-square fit in uv plane

evidence.quote: the best bit (reduced $\chi^2$=0.5) Gaussian profile

validation.value: Consistent with imfit and sextractor on cleaned image

evidence.quote: We obtain consistent results if we instead using the imfit algorithm or sextractor on the cleaned image.

analysis_steps.goal: Extract CO(3-2) spectrum and line properties

method.value: Iterative procedure: weight-averaged map over best-guess width, curve-of-growth aperture, clean to 2 sigma, Gaussian fit, update FWHM until convergence

evidence.quote: Next the extracted spectrum is fitted with a Gaussian profile and the frequency width used for obtaining the averaged map is updated to be the FWHM of the spectral fit.

key_parameters.value: line flux contained within 2'' circular radius

evidence.quote: all the line flux is contained within a circular radius of 2$''$

fitting.value: Gaussian fit; errors from fit and Monte Carlo injection of model profiles in random cube regions

evidence.quote: We create fake spectra by injecting model profile into spectra extracted from randomly selected regions of the data cube

validation.value: Fit errors consistent with Monte Carlo errors

evidence.quote: The errors are estimates from the fit, and they are consistent with the errors derived from a Monte Carlo simulation.

analysis_steps.goal: CO luminosity and brightness temperature ratio

method.value: Solomon & Vanden Bout relation for L'CO; ratio with ATCA CO(1-0)

evidence.quote: $L^\prime_{\rm CO}=3.25\times10^7 S_{\rm CO}\Delta v\nu_{\rm obs}^{-2}D_{\rm L}^2(1+z)^{-3}$

method.value: imfit on averaged map with bias correction from 36000 injected models, plus uv-plane chi-square Gaussian fit; uv-based result adopted

evidence.quote: We therefore adopt the *uv*-based measurement for the $^{12}$CO size.

key_parameters.value: 36000 injected models, peak SNR 1-10, radius up to 2''

evidence.quote: In total we inject 36000 models with the peak SNR, major axis, minor axis, and positional angle all randomized

fitting.value: chi-square Gaussian fit to averaged visibilities vs uv distance

evidence.quote: perform $\chi^2$ fitting assuming a Gaussian profile

validation.value: Image-plane and uv results agree; injection tests for bias (3%) and scatter (20%)

evidence.quote: We find a 3% upward bias in median (0.028$\pm$0.007) and a 20% scatter.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit SINFONI lines and measure integrated Halpha properties and size

method.value: Chi-square fit of Halpha+[NII]+[SII] Gaussians with linear continuum over 1.9-2.2 um; AICc model selection; curve-of-growth aperture of 1.8'' radius

evidence.quote: The spectra are fit with four Gaussian models, in which all include a linear continuum component with the slope and normalization allowed free.

key_parameters.value: [NII] doublet ratio fixed to 3; skylines masked; significance Delta chi2>25 ([SII] additional >9)

evidence.quote: a fit with line components is considered significant if the fit, compared to a simple continuum-only model, has a lower AICc and provides a $\chi^2$ improvement of $\Delta\chi^2>25$

fitting.value: Minimum chi-square with Monte Carlo errors

evidence.quote: The errors are derived using Monte Carlo simulations similar to those used for measuring the errors of the CO emission.
The model selection is determined based on the Akaike information criterion.

method.value: Adaptive binning (1,3x3,5x5 spaxels); arctan rotation curve fit with emcee; kinemetry K_asym

evidence.quote: we run emcee, a Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) ensemble sampler (cite: Foreman-Mackey:2013aa), to explore the parameter space and derive uncertainties.

key_parameters.value: Fit v_asym sin(i) as a single parameter; centre and r_t within SINFONI FoV; PA 0-180 deg

evidence.quote: Because $v_{asym}$ and $i$ are essentially degenerate for our data quality we treat $v_{asym}{\rm sin}(i)$ as a single parameter.

fitting.value: Maximum likelihood with emcee; centre perturbed within MCMC errors for kinemetry

evidence.quote: We fit the 2D model to the measured data based on maximum likelihood

validation.value: Reduced chi2=14.8 indicates poor disk fit; K_asym compared with Shapiro et al. criterion

evidence.quote: The reduced $\chi^2_\nu=14.8$, indicating a relatively poor fit to the data and suggesting ALESS67.1 is not a pure rotating disk.

analysis_steps.goal: Derive alpha_CO dynamically and via gas-to-dust ratio

method.value: Mdyn from turbulence-corrected vc at r_e; subtract stellar mass and 15% dark matter to get gas mass; divide by L'CO(1-0). Cross-check with gas-to-dust ratio from metallicity (N2 calibration)

evidence.quote: the gas mass is derived by subtracting stellar and dark-matter mass from the dynamical mass

key_parameters.value: dark matter fraction 15%; <sin^2 i>=2/3; median sigma 154±5 km/s

evidence.quote: so we adopt 15%

assumptions.value: Gas and stars share same half-light radius; constant velocity dispersion

evidence.quote: we assume the gas and stars have the same r$_e$ given this is what we find

validation.value: Gas-to-dust method gives alpha_CO=1.4±0.7, consistent with dynamical estimate

evidence.quote: we calculate a gas mass of $(5.5\pm0.6)\times 10^{10} M_\odot$, and therefore a $\alpha_{\rm CO,GDR}=1.4\pm0.7$

method.value: 0.5'' concentric rings centred on 870um peak; maps convolved to CO beam; SFR from L_IR and Halpha (Kennicutt 1998), alpha_CO=0.8

evidence.quote: we construct concentric rings with a width of 0$\ensuremath{''}$5 ($\sim$4 kpc) for each ring and centered at the peak of the 870 $\mu$m continuum.

assumptions.value: Chabrier IMF; alpha_CO=0.8; Halpha not extinction corrected

evidence.quote: We assume a Chabrier initial mass function (cite: Chabrier:2003aa) and adopt 0.8 for $\alpha_{\rm CO}$ in order to make comparisons with other studies.

findings_qualitative.value: Halpha and 870um dust emission are spatially offset (0.4''), with H-alpha ~3x more extended

evidence.quote: The sky separation between the peaks of the H$\alpha$ and 870 $\mu$m continuum is 0$\ensuremath{''}$4

findings_qualitative.value: CO and Halpha kinematics are in broad agreement

evidence.quote: In general we find that the kinematics of both HII regions as traced by the optical emission lines and molecular gas as traced by $^{12}$CO(J=3-2) are in broad agreement.

claims.hypothesis: ALESS67.1 is a pure rotating disk
claims.experiment: Arctan disk fit and kinemetry of Halpha velocity and dispersion maps
claims.finding: Not a pure rotating disk; likely a merger

evidence.quote: Dynamical modelling of the optical emission lines suggests that ALESS67.1 is not a pure rotating disk but a merger

claims.hypothesis: Dust, CO gas, Halpha and stars have similar sizes
claims.experiment: Half-light radii measured for each tracer
claims.result: Dust 1.2 kpc vs 5-6.6 kpc for others
claims.finding: Dust is a factor 4-6 more compact and offset

evidence.quote: We therefore find that the dust continuum has a factor of 4–6 smaller size than that of strong optical emission lines, NIR continuum, and $^{12}$CO($J$=3-2)

claims.hypothesis: Spatial mismatch of dust and UV explains offset on the IRX-beta diagram
claims.experiment: Compare L_IR/L_UV and beta with image overlays
claims.result: Source lies above local relations with decoupled dust and UV
claims.finding: Geometry plausibly part of the cause

evidence.quote: confirms the hypothesis that the deviation from the IRX-$\beta$ relationship is caused, at least partially, by the different distributions between dust and UV

claims.hypothesis: alpha_CO in this SMG is low like mergers
claims.experiment: Dynamical method and gas-to-dust ratio method

evidence.quote: Using the dynamical method we derive the CO-to-H$_2$ conversion factor of $\alpha_{\rm CO} = 1.8\pm1.0$, supported by the estimates based on the gas-to-dust ratio method.

claims.hypothesis: Star-formation efficiency is uniform within the galaxy
claims.experiment: Resolved ring-by-ring Sigma_SFR vs Sigma_H2 with alpha_CO=0.8
claims.result: Core lies with mergers, outskirts with normal SFGs

evidence.quote: The core shares the same locus as mergers whereas the outskirts lie close to the SFGs selected in UV/optical, suggesting different star formation efficiency within one galaxy.

why_this_data.value: ALESS67.1 is covered by all necessary follow-up observations and is representative of the ALESS sample

evidence.quote: ALESS67.1 is one of the few SMGs so far that is covered by all the necessary follow-up observations, and it is representative of the ALESS sample

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Rotation-dominated criterion (vmax-vmin)/2sigma=0.4 suggested a disk, but detailed modelling used instead

evidence.quote: However, the availability of the 2D velocity map allows us to conduct detail kinematic modelling to more reliably differentiate rotating systems from mergers.

limitations_admitted.value: CO detection is only ~3 sigma peak SNR so 2D CO kinematics and central detail are limited

evidence.quote: Our $^{12}$CO(J=3-2) detection does not have high enough SNR to produce 2D kinematic maps like H$\alpha$
so the nature of ALESS67.2 remains inconclusive

referee_caveats_inferred: Single object, so generality of size contrast is uncertain
SINFONI astrometry uncertainty (0.2-0.3'') comparable to dust-Halpha offset
alpha_CO from dynamical method relies on assumed dark matter fraction, inclination average and point-mass approximation despite merger evidence
Sigma_SFR and Sigma_H2 rings depend on assumed alpha_CO=0.8 and uncorrected Halpha
